filmHorreur.modeDuoMeta: Taking turns, or each on your own phone
filmHorreur.relaisDebut: Answer all the situations, then pass the phone.
filmHorreur.relaisSuite: {{nom}} is done. Your turn, no peeking at their answers!
filmHorreur.verdictEquivalent: Two different answers, the same fate.
filmHorreur.ecartsTitre: Where you didn't react the same way
filmHorreur.modesDesc: Fifteen situations, from arriving at the cabin to the end credits. Solo, you find out how long you last. As a couple, each of you answers separately, and we find out who dies first.
filmHorreur.modeDuoDesc: Taking turns on the same phone, or each on your own with remote mode.
filmHorreur.setupTitreSolo: How long would you last in a horror movie?
filmHorreur.setupDescSolo: A cabin rented for the weekend, a forbidden cellar, footsteps in the attic, a book that should have stayed shut. Fifteen situations, four reactions each time: the result tells you at which minute you leave the film, and why.
filmHorreur.setupDescDuo: Enter your first names. The first player answers the fifteen situations, passes the phone, and the second answers in turn. At the end, your two survival times on the same line, and the name of the first victim.
filmHorreur.resLibelleSolo: In a horror movie, you last...
filmHorreur.duoEgal: You die together, after {{v1}}. It's almost romantic.
filmHorreur.duoSurvie: You both make it to the end credits. The killer leaves empty-handed!
filmHorreur.verdictDifferent: {{nom}} doesn't do so well on this one.
filmHorreur.noteFin: A movie runs two and a half hours at most: at 2 h 30, you survived the whole movie, end credits included.
filmHorreur.r1_d: You're the person who goes down to the basement saying “it's probably the wind”. The movie starts, your name rolls in the credits, and it's already over. The audience didn't even have time to learn your name.
filmHorreur.r1_a: Next time, stay in the car. Better: don't go away for the weekend.
filmHorreur.r2_d: You survive the opening, just long enough for people to get a bit attached to you, then you go check that noise in the attic. The audience screams, but they knew.
filmHorreur.r2_a: Never split from the group. And don't read anything out loud.
filmHorreur.r3_t: Dead in the middle of the movie
filmHorreur.r3_d: You have the right reflexes half the time. You last a good hour, you make reasonable choices, and then you turn around to check the killer is really down.
filmHorreur.r3_a: When the bad guy is on the ground, you don't check. You leave.
filmHorreur.r4_d: You make it to the final act. You locked the doors, kept the keys in your hand, refused the shortcut. But there's always that last scene, the one where everyone drops their keys.
filmHorreur.r4_a: Keys go in your hand, not in your pocket.
filmHorreur.r5_d: You make it to the end credits. You understood the rules: you don't split up, you don't go down to the basement, you don't read anything out loud, and when the car won't start, you had a plan. The movie tells your story.
filmHorreur.r5_a: Watch out for the sequel: in the second movie, it's always the survivor of the first who dies first.
filmHorreur.q1: You arrive at the cabin rented for the weekend. The owner hands you the keys and says: 'Whatever you do, don't go down to the cellar.'
filmHorreur.q1a: I go down to the cellar as soon as his back is turned, torch between my teeth
filmHorreur.q1b: I ask him why, three times, until he leaves muttering
filmHorreur.q1c: I note the information, lock the cellar door and keep the key on me
filmHorreur.q1d: I get back in the car: we'll find a hotel
filmHorreur.q2: 11 p.m. Footsteps in the attic, right above your head. There's nobody in the attic.
filmHorreur.q2a: I go up to look, in my socks, with the flickering torch
filmHorreur.q2b: I send my partner to look, and wait downstairs with the phone
filmHorreur.q2c: I lock the hatch, turn on every light, and we all sleep in the living room
filmHorreur.q2d: Everyone in the car: we sleep somewhere else, now
filmHorreur.q3: The phone shows zero bars. The landline's cord has been cut.
filmHorreur.q3a: I go off alone into the forest looking for signal, shouting 'hello?'
filmHorreur.q3b: I tell myself it's the countryside, it's normal, and pour myself another drink
filmHorreur.q3c: I work out the shortest road to the village and keep the car keys on me
filmHorreur.q3d: A cut cord means someone cut it: we leave right now, without turning off the lights
filmHorreur.q4: In a dusty box, a leather-bound book covered in symbols. One page is marked.
filmHorreur.q4a: I read the marked page out loud, in the movie voice, to make the others laugh
filmHorreur.q4b: I leaf through it in silence, and keep the marked page for later
filmHorreur.q4c: I close it, put it back exactly where it was, and don't touch it again
filmHorreur.q4d: I burn it in the fireplace, and keep an eye on the fireplace
filmHorreur.q5: The dog is barking at the corner of the garden, hackles up, and won't stop.
filmHorreur.q5a: I go and see what's there, in my pyjamas, telling him 'you're silly'
filmHorreur.q5b: I shout at him to shut up and go back to sleep
filmHorreur.q5c: I call him back, lock the door and turn off the living room light
filmHorreur.q5d: I take the dog under my arm and we go and sleep in the car, doors locked
filmHorreur.q6: On the road to the village, a man in overalls offers a shortcut through the woods. 'Twenty minutes less.'
filmHorreur.q6a: I accept, he seems nice, and I let him lead the way
filmHorreur.q6b: I accept, but I walk behind him with a rock in my hand
filmHorreur.q6c: I politely decline and stick to the main road, even if it's longer
filmHorreur.q6d: I decline, turn back, and describe his face to the others so everyone recognises him
filmHorreur.q7: A friend is missing. The group wants to split up to search faster.
filmHorreur.q7a: I head alone for the abandoned barn; that's where I'd have gone in his place
filmHorreur.q7b: I stay alone in the house, lights off, 'so he sees me when he gets back'
filmHorreur.q7c: I go with the strongest person in the group, and we keep the others in sight
filmHorreur.q7d: Nobody splits up: the five of us search together, holding each other's sleeves if we have to
filmHorreur.q8: In the bathroom, the mirror is covered in steam. Nobody has taken a shower. A word is appearing on it.
filmHorreur.q8a: I write 'hi' underneath, for a laugh
filmHorreur.q8b: I wipe the steam off and don't look behind me
filmHorreur.q8c: I back out of the bathroom and wedge the door with a chair
filmHorreur.q8d: I leave the house, full stop. I'll use the toilet outside
filmHorreur.q9: In the empty house, someone whispers your name. In your voice, a little.
filmHorreur.q9a: I answer 'yes?' and walk towards the sound
filmHorreur.q9b: I pretend I didn't hear anything and turn up the TV
filmHorreur.q9c: I grab the longest kitchen knife and back towards the door
filmHorreur.q9d: I go out through the nearest window, even if it's shut
filmHorreur.q10: You run to the car. It won't start.
filmHorreur.q10a: I open the bonnet in the dark, alone, torch in my mouth
filmHorreur.q10b: I turn the key ten times shouting 'come on, come on, come on'
filmHorreur.q10c: We go back in, barricade, and wait for daylight with everything that cuts
filmHorreur.q10d: I'd parked the second car at the end of the track, keys in my pocket from the start
filmHorreur.q11: The porcelain doll from the wardrobe is now on your pillow. It's looking at the door.
filmHorreur.q11a: I sit her facing me and say goodnight, she's cute
filmHorreur.q11b: I put her back in the wardrobe, and block the wardrobe with the chest of drawers
filmHorreur.q11c: I put her outside, in the bin, lid closed, bin at the bottom of the garden
filmHorreur.q11d: I'm not sleeping in that room anymore, or in that house
filmHorreur.q12: The landline rings, even though its cord is cut. A voice: 'I'm inside the house.'
filmHorreur.q12a: I ask 'who is this?' and wait for the answer
filmHorreur.q12b: I hang up and hide in the wardrobe, the one that creaks
filmHorreur.q12c: I go out through the nearest door and run to the neighbours'
filmHorreur.q12d: I never picked up: I'd been outside since the footsteps in the attic
filmHorreur.q13: The killer is on the floor, motionless, his mask beside him.
filmHorreur.q13a: I go closer to see his face and check he's dead
filmHorreur.q13b: I take his weapon and turn my back on him to talk to the others
filmHorreur.q13c: I run, without looking back, all the way to the road
filmHorreur.q13d: I make sure he won't get up again, then I leave, without a glance
filmHorreur.q14: One car left, your keys, and a noise right behind you.
filmHorreur.q14a: I turn round to see what it is
filmHorreur.q14b: I drop the keys, obviously, and feel around for them
filmHorreur.q14c: I run to the car, key already in hand, without turning round
filmHorreur.q14d: I've been at the wheel for ten minutes, engine running, doors locked
filmHorreur.q15: You're invited back to the cabin 'to get closure'.
filmHorreur.q15a: I go, with the same friends, the same weekend, the same owner
filmHorreur.q15b: I go, but in daytime, and I stay in the car
filmHorreur.q15c: I refuse, and I sell the book, the doll and everything that came from there
filmHorreur.q15d: I never set foot in a house with a cellar again
